title: Rabies Risk Demands Evidence, Quarantine, and Dog-Trade Abolition
excerpt: Rabies kills after symptoms begin. Unverified claims cannot excuse weak quarantine, illicit transport, or stolen companion animals. Vietnam needs enforceable reform and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
Every possible rabies exposure carries a brutal deadline: wash any bite or scratch with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, then seek urgent medical assessment before symptoms appear. Once clinical symptoms develop, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. World Health Organization guidance makes this clear.

That fact does not prove every dog in commercial circulation carries rabies. It does prove why uninspected slaughter, illegal transport, and quarantine evasion demand enforcement. Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains are separate dimensions of broken biosecurity. Neither permits officials or operators to gamble with family safety.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

“Farm-raised” is a claim, not a quarantine record. Without documented origin, veterinary inspection, vaccination history, and lawful transport, buyers cannot verify where animals came from or whether stolen companions entered the chain. A missing pet is not inventory. It is a family loss, and theft for profit deserves investigation and punishment.

Evidence must govern every defense

Available reporting here does not verify a particular cyanide seizure, court conviction, or claim that no dog farms exist. Those claims require named records, dates, locations, and agencies. Precision strengthens reform: expose documented poison bait, illegal transport, stolen pets, and enforcement failures when records establish them; reject unsupported excuses when they do not.

Vietnamese communities can close the gap

National public-health targets and SDE’s campaign demand are distinct. Public authorities must strengthen vaccination, exposure response, quarantine, inspection, and transport enforcement. SDE calls for complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Vietnamese families, veterinarians, local officials, and animal defenders can lead that change.

Sign the national petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Add your name to a public demand for action and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.

Rabies leaves no room for unverified trade claims or weak quarantine.

• WHO: rabies is virtually 100% fatal once clinical symptoms appear.
• After possible exposure: wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes; seek urgent medical care for post-exposure prophylaxis.
• Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. Risk centers on infected saliva entering bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes.
• Illegal transport, uninspected slaughter, quarantine evasion, and pet theft require evidence-based enforcement.
• Separate household exposure incidents from commercial supply-chain claims. Do not invent links.
• Public health enforcement and SDE’s demand differ: SDE calls for complete abolition by 2030.

Vietnamese communities can protect families and companion animals through stronger traceability, veterinary control, and abolition.
